# Lute

> Lute is a statically analyzable narrative language for branching games: `.lute` documents compile to a versioned JSON IR plus CEL. Write dialogue, quests, cinematic beats, and relational world state; check reachability, simulate outcomes, and compile before you ship. Language version 0.26.0.

Lute is deliberately non-Turing: every document is a finite, terminating artifact, so the checker can prove reachability, definite-assignment, and envelope properties instead of guessing. The CLI (`lute`) is a headless checker, compiler, and preview tool; `lute context --json` emits the project-resolved authoring surface an AI or human needs to write valid Lute, and `lute check --json` gives a machine-readable diagnostic loop. Content vocabulary is the project's, not the compiler's: since language 0.9.0 the core declares seven *slots* (`emotion`, `action`, `anchor`, `mood`, `volume`, `musicAction`, `vfxType`) and ships zero members, so every `emotion=`/`action=`/`::music{mood}` value must be declared by the project first — an undeclared slot is the error `E-DOMAIN-UNKNOWN`. Below, each link points to a single documentation page on <https://lute-lang.vercel.app>.

## Docs

- [Installation](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/getting-started/installation/): Install the `lute` CLI with bunx, a global bun install, or from Rust source, then verify the toolchain.
- [Try Lute (playground)](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/playground/): A fully client-side browser playground — the Lute core compiled to WebAssembly — with live diagnostics, the compiled JSON IR, and a mock-driven trace over one self-contained core-profile document.
- [Write your first scene](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/getting-started/first-scene/): Build one small, real Lute scene from an empty file step by step, running `lute` at every step.
- [Learning paths](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/getting-started/learning-paths/): Role-first reading routes — scenario writer, narrative programmer, engine integrator, plugin author, AI tooling developer — each an ordered list of existing pages.
- [Build an investigation](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/getting-started/build-an-investigation/): A first-project tutorial walking the worked investigation example end to end — manifest, schema, facts + Datalog, an interrogation hub, a quest, after: sequencing, check-project and what it proves about relational fact guards (W-FACT-GUARANTEED, dead guards), scenario reach, two trace mocks, compile.
- [Is Lute right for you?](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/getting-started/when-to-use/): Honest fit/no-fit selection guidance — the projects and teams Lute serves well today versus the ones it does not fit yet.
- [Cheatsheet](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/reference/cheatsheet/): One dense page to keep open while writing Lute 0.26.0 — every construct as a checked snippet (project layout and `defaults:` hoist, schema with def shorthand, frontmatter per kind, lines, choices/hubs/`::next`/`::end`, `<match>`/`<when is>` with ranges, `::set`/`::assert`/`::retract`/`::accept`, CEL tiers and functions, beats (`also`, `select: sequence`, lore `<beat>` bundles, `share` keys, bundle `after=`), quests (`by=` / `until=` deadlines, objective targets, `activate="accept"`, `complete="any"`, `accept="external"`), exclusive relations (`excludes:`), the clock (`clock:`, `once: day|slot`, `advance:`), lore entries, occasions, `prev.run`, cast, reward `credits`, components, timelines), the CLI with mock/test/play-script formats (engine steps, save seeds, expect: including `presented`), `lute beats` / `lute calendar`, the ~25 diagnostics authors hit most, and gotchas. Since dsl 0.24.0 also: the declared clock (`clock:`, `clock.*`, `once: day`/`slot`, labels, `%`, `::set when=`), quest structure (`activate="accept"`, `complete="any"`, `failedBy`, `until=`, `judge: before`, `::accept at="nextRun"`, `<on event target>`), sub-kinds and `per:` state, `_` and `countDistinct` in rules, cast `present:`/`emotions:`, `::clear`, `{{x:ordinal}}`, `effects: true` components, and `advance:`/`include:`/`bridges:` in play scripts. The dsl 0.25.0 and 0.26.0 additions (`add:`, kind targets, directive `when=`, component defaults and `@@who`, rule counts) are marked inline.
- [Many authors, one project](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/guides/multi-author/): How a lead and several area writers share one project (dsl 0.26.0) — ownership by directory, kinds assembled with `add:`, `defaults.uses` globs and `questTier`, id conventions, cast display names (`W-DISPLAY-NAME-DUP`, `sharedName`), shared components with `@@who`, contract beats versus `check-project --wip`, `include:` steps with hand-off `expect:` and `advance: { to }` / `expect.clock`, the merge gates (`check-project --deny-warnings`, `lute test`, `lute beats`, `lute refs`), and what the tool catches and does not.
- [Frontmatter & profiles](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/language/frontmatter-and-profiles/): The YAML frontmatter block that opens every `.lute` document, plus the profile/plugins capability selectors.
- [Content vocabulary](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/language/vocabulary/): The seven content-vocabulary slots the compiler declares without members — the three routes that declare members (a document's own frontmatter `enums:`, a project schema imported through `uses:`/`extends:`, a plugin's `enums` export), their precedence, and the required `exits:`/`default:` member semantics. A single-file `lute check` applies the nearest `lute.project.yaml` above the file; `compile`, `trace`, and `context` need `--project <dir>` (or use `check-project`), else they run core-only and a plugin-declared slot reports `E-DOMAIN-UNKNOWN`.
- [Dialogue & cast](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/language/dialogue-and-cast/): Content lines — the `@speaker` syntax — plus delivery flags, line attributes, interpolation, and the cast: a schema `cast:` or plugin `cast` export makes an undeclared speaker `E-CAST-UNKNOWN` (dsl 0.23.0). Since dsl 0.24.0 a cast entry may declare `present:` (a line whose guards do not imply it is `W-CAST-ABSENT`) and per-speaker `emotions:`; `::auto`/`::camera` are checked against the cast; `{{x:ordinal}}` renders ordinals and an enum path renders its member label. dsl 0.25.0: a reserved relation's `changedOn:` narrows cast `assume: true` after its occasions; `{{x:ordinalWord}}`.
- [Core directives](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/language/directives/): The nine `lute.core` directives — the staging leaves `::bg`, `::music`, `::sfx`, `::camera` and friends plus the walk terminator `::end` — their attributes, timing keys, and the wait model. Since dsl 0.24.0 the core has ten directives: `::clear` empties the stage; quoted attribute values decode XML character references. dsl 0.26.0: `when=` on `::use`, `::accept`, `::assert`, `::retract` and plugin directives (refused on built-in-lowered ones, `E-UNKNOWN-ATTR`).
- [Branch, match & when](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/language/branch-match-when/): The logic layer — player-driven `<branch>` menus and state-driven `<match>`/`<when>`/`<otherwise>` arms. A beat/entry `when` narrows its body (dsl 0.24.0): `isSet` proves reads, ruled-out arms are `E-ARM-DEAD`, and `<match on="@def">` takes the def's domain.
- [Choices & hubs](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/language/choices-and-hubs/): Choice mechanics — `when` guards and the `into=` run-record sugar — plus revisit `<hub>` conversations and the no-dead-end guarantee, and the `<hub prompt>` question shown with a hub's options.
- [Timeline & property tracks](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/language/timeline-and-property-tracks/): The `<timeline>` multi-track choreography block — a local clock, subject/channel/property tracks, and the one-writer-per-track rule.
- [Components & extends](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/language/components-and-extends/): Reusable content components invoked with `::use`, and `extends` schema composition with base-layer override precedence A component `string` param interpolated as `{{@p}}` ships each call site's own sentence (dsl 0.23.0). Since dsl 0.24.0 a component declaring `effects: true` may `::set`/`::assert`/`::retract`, checked at each `::use`, and a `speaker` param takes a cast id. dsl 0.26.0: `@@who:` speaks as a `speaker` param, params take `default:`, a component reads its own directive results, `{{…}}` in string arguments and `as=@who` behave as in direct text, and `::use{… when=}` guards the whole expansion.
- [Definitions & params](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/language/params/): Named typed CEL macros declared in `defs`, referenced as `@name`, and parameterized as `@name(args)`. An atomic def argument splices without parentheses; a def is checked where it is used; defs work in rule `cel()` guards (`E-RULE-GUARD-DEF`).
- [Quests & scenes](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/language/quests-and-scenes/): The time-axis document kinds — scenes sequenced with `after:`, and quests with objectives, derived completion, and lifecycle-event reactions — plus the optional quest-document `id:` that names a quest chain and `<quest tier="run">` quests that reset every run — plus `<objective by>` deadlines that fail an objective the first time they hold and `<objective on target>` objectives judged only for one target (dsl 0.23.0). Since dsl 0.24.0: `<quest activate="accept">` subquests, `<quest complete="any">` alternatives (the rest fail `superseded`), read-only `quest.<id>.failedBy` / `objectives.<o>.failed`, `by=` judged at every settle beside the place-bound `until=`, occasion `judge: before`, `::accept{at="nextRun"}`, `<on event target>`, bundle beats as `after:` predecessors, `W-QUEST-NEVER-ACCEPTED`. dsl 0.25.0: `<quest accept="external">`, `[subquest]` and `[start]` graph anchors; a test mock no longer counts as an acceptance. dsl 0.26.0: `defaults.questTier`, handler `::accept`s applied by trace/test, project-wide `accepts:` and `engine: { accept }` in plays.
- [Lore entries](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/language/lore-entries/): The `kind: lore` document — `<entry>` declarations the engine looks up instead of plays (item descriptions, found notes, inscriptions, codex pages, barks), with state-dependent text, knowledge revealed by `::assert` on the first read only, the reserved `entry.<id>.read` path, document bundles (`id:` + `series:`), the user-tier `entry.<id>.everRead`, and `once` entry beats, and scene-like `<beat>` blocks bundled beside entries in one lore document (dsl 0.23.0). Since dsl 0.24.0 entries take `once="day"|"slot"`, an entry `target=` on an untargeted occasion is metadata, and a guard assuming `entry.X.read` knows the facts X asserted. dsl 0.25.0: `share=` on entry beats; bundle beats take `after=`. dsl 0.26.0: kind targets (`target="kind:X"`, `occasion.target`), `W-ENTRY-WRITE-REREAD`, and `<doc>.<entry>` ids in play and test.
- [Beats](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/language/beats/): Scenes and lore entries that answer engine occasions (dsl 0.21.0 – 0.23.0) — the scene frontmatter keys `on` / `target` / `when` / `priority` / `once`, the entry attributes `on=` / `priority=` / `once=`, selection order (priority, then project order), `select: first` / `all` / `sequence`, `also: true` side beats, scene-like `<beat>` bundles in lore documents (canonical id `<document id>.<beat id>`), how the checker decides a `when` (per-path contradictions, `check-project --wip`), plugin-declared occasions and their target domains, and `E-BEAT-ATTR` / `E-OCCASION-UNKNOWN` / `E-BEAT-UNREACHABLE` / `W-BEAT-SHADOWED` / `W-BEAT-PRIORITY-TIE` / `W-BEAT-ONCE-RUN-USER`. dsl 0.24.0 adds `once: day` / `once: slot` under a declared clock and bundle beats as `after:` predecessors. dsl 0.25.0: shared spends (`share`) and bundle `<beat after=…>`. dsl 0.26.0: `target="kind:X"` kind targets with `occasion.target`, a clearer `W-BEAT-PRIORITY-TIE`, and `covered by` in `lute beats`.
- [The clock](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/language/clock/): A declared day × slot clock (dsl 0.24.0) — the schema `clock:` over two `owner: engine` paths, the read-only `clock.index` / `clock.weekday` / `clock.weekdayLabel`, `once: day` / `once: slot` beats and entries, enum member display labels, integer `%`, the guarded `::set{… when="…"}`, moving time with `lute play` `advance:` / `include:` steps, the `lute calendar --axis clock` grid, and `E-CLOCK-DECL` / `E-ENUM-LABEL-NOT-MEMBER`.
- [Imports (uses:)](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/language/imports/): How a scene imports its shared state schema with `uses:`, the plain-YAML `.schema.yaml` files, and the DAG discipline shared by `uses`/`extends`/components.
- [The state model](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/state/state-model/): Lute's tiered scalar state — the run, user, app, and scene lifetime namespaces, `owner: engine` paths (`E-ENGINE-OWNED-WRITE`), and the path-sensitive definite-assignment rules, and the reserved read-only `prev.run.<path>` — the value a run path had when the previous run ended. Since dsl 0.24.0: paths typed by a named enum render member labels, `per: <kind>` declares one path per entity member (with per-member defaults), and `clock.*` / `quest.<id>.failedBy` are reserved read-only.
- [Facts and Datalog](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/state/facts-and-datalog/): The relational fact layer — declared entities and relations, ground facts asserted and retracted as deltas, a total Datalog derivation layer, and how check-project decides relational guards (impossible / guaranteed / possible from the may and must fact sets; E-ARM-DEAD, E-ENTRY-UNREACHABLE, W-FACT-GUARANTEED). Since dsl 0.24.0: entity sub-kinds (`subsetOf:`), `_` in rule bodies, `countDistinct`, `@def`s and `run.approval[P]` in rule guards, `E-RELATION-RESERVED-NAME`, `W-RELATION-UNREAD`. dsl 0.25.0: exclusive relations (`excludes:`, `E-FACT-EXCLUSIVE`, `E-RULE-EXCLUSIVE`) and `changedOn:`. dsl 0.26.0: `count` / `countDistinct` in rule bodies (`E-RULE-AGGREGATE-CYCLE`), `add:` to extend a kind across schemas, sub-kind members implied in the parent, duplicate members `E-ENTITY-KIND-SHAPE`.
- [CEL expressions](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/state/cel/): The restricted Lute-CEL profile behind every condition and assignment, the fact-query surface it admits, and how it compiles. Integer `%` joined the profile in dsl 0.24.0 (`E-CEL-TYPE` on a non-integer), with `countDistinct` and the `{{x:ordinal}}` interpolation hint.
- [State schemas](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/state/schemas/): The shared, imported source of truth for run/user/app state and defs — the schema document shape, `uses`, and `extends`. dsl 0.24.0 adds the schema keys `clock:`, enum `labels:`, `subsetOf:`, `per:`, and cast `present:`/`emotions:`; `W-DEF-UNUSED` flags a dead def. dsl 0.26.0: `E-STATE-DECL-CONFLICT` across documents, `add:`, `defaults.uses` globs.
- [The scene graph and after:](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/connectivity/scene-graph/): How Lute assembles a project-wide prerequisite graph from each document's `after` declaration and the restricted formula grammar. dsl 0.25.0: bundle beat `after=` and anchor edge kinds.
- [Reachability](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/connectivity/reachability/): How Lute proves whether a node has a satisfiable route under the `after` graph — the Reachable/Unreachable/Unknown verdicts.
- [Guaranteed / Possible envelopes](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/connectivity/envelopes/): The per-node available-state analysis — the Guaranteed and Possible tables over run/user state, the guaranteed-facts table beside them, and the Possible-minus-Guaranteed warning.
- [CLI reference](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/tooling/cli/): Every `lute` subcommand — init, new, check, check-project, compile, compile-stream, run, play, trace, test, scenario (+ `knowledge`), beats, calendar, context, tag, fix, lore, doctor, loc, catalog refresh, version — with flags, NDJSON/output shapes, and exit codes. dsl 0.24.0 adds `--expand` on trace/beats, calendar `visited()`/`clock` axes, `--occasion O@path` and `--facts`, the knowledge guard-slot report, `lute lore` Derived sections, and `bridges:` answers in run/test/trace. dsl 0.25.0: scenario `[subquest]`/`[start]` anchors, entry nodes and `unanchoredHints`. dsl 0.26.0: `lute refs`, `scenario --facts`, `beats` covered-by, `doctor --strict`, `--wip` for component-only producers, trace/test following `::next`, failing ineligible walks, and parallel `lute test`.
- [Playing a story](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/tooling/play/): Occasions and beats (dsl 0.21.0) — how a project says which piece of story answers which engine moment — and `lute play`, the reference player that walks a scripted sequence of raised occasions and `engine:` writes through a whole project, starting from a save, and prints every candidate, its verdict, and the winner; `expect:` assertions make a play a test `lute test` runs (dsl 0.22.0); since 0.23.0 `select: sequence` lists, `also` beats, bundle beats, `by=` deadlines and targeted objectives, `prev.run` at `newRun`, reward credits, and the `presented:` expectation. dsl 0.24.0 adds `advance:` (a declared clock, with day-boundary raises) and `include:` steps, `bridges:` answers, quest structure transcripts, step `expect.options`, `prevRun` at `newRun`, and `--explain` provenance. dsl 0.25.0: `✗ exclusive` halts, shared-spend verdicts, bridge fields content does not read may be omitted. dsl 0.26.0: `advance: { to }`, step `expect.clock`, `engine: { accept }`, kind-target beats, `<doc>.<entry>` ids, attribute-free transcript needles.
- [Story overviews](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/tooling/overviews/): See who can say what, when, across a whole project (dsl 0.23.0) — `lute beats` prints each occasion's beat ladder with priority, `once`, `when` and the `check-project` verdicts; `lute calendar` evaluates play's own eligibility at every cell of a grid of state values (`--axis run.day=1..7`) from a save and names the beats never eligible; `lute scenario knowledge` traces every fact-guarded condition through rules to the documents that assert its facts. dsl 0.24.0 adds calendar `clock` and `visited()` axes, per-occasion axes and a `--facts` presence grid, the never-presented list, and `--expand`. dsl 0.25.0: the `share` column, every defeater derivation route, and unanchored beat hints. dsl 0.26.0: `covered by` fallbacks and `kind:` ladders in `lute beats`, `lute scenario --facts` producer edges, rule counts in `knowledge`.
- [Runtime contract](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/tooling/runtime-contract/): The engine-side contract — what Lute emits (a versioned JSON IR plus CEL) and what an engine adapter must implement to play it: the command loop, CEL evaluation, facts, quest lifecycle, `::end` termination, and typed bridges.
- [Capability permissions](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/tooling/capability-permissions/): Prospective, Unreleased compile-time ceilings over authored directives, state/fact writes, bridges, rewards, and quests — absent versus explicit-empty fields, conjunctive project/profile/host layering, trusted `--permission-profile`, `E-PERMISSION-*`, filtered context/LSP surfaces, and the explicit runtime-sandbox boundary.
- [Streaming continuation compiler](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/tooling/continuation-compiler/): Append ordinary final-shot Lute body source to a frozen checked scene template; consume flushed full-artifact snapshots while retaining the numeric runtime cursor, state, facts, and control-flow state; understand framing, EOF versus authored `end`, address-padding compatibility, prefix rejection, cumulative compile cost, and the lower-level parser API.
- [Tracing guide](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/tooling/tracing/): Preview a scene before shipping — seeding state, facts, choices, events, accepts and save history via flags or a mock YAML file, Datalog derivation by default (`derive: false` / `--no-derive`), and the `E-TRACE-*` refusals Raising an occasion for a target (`occasions: [talk@npc.maud]`) and presenting one bundle beat with `--beat` (dsl 0.23.0). dsl 0.24.0 adds `bridges:` answers (an unanswered call is unresolved, never defaulted), `expect.accepts`, hub `offered:`, and `--expand`. dsl 0.25.0: exclusive-relation refusals and omittable unread bridge fields. dsl 0.26.0: `::next` followed, handler accepts applied, `state: { occasion.target }` for kind beats.
- [Linting](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/tooling/linting/): `lute lint` — advisory, per-project editorial lints (`L-*` codes) configured in `lute.lint.yaml`: core rules, custom rules, plugin `lints` exports, metric tables, exit codes. dsl 0.26.0: `W-DISPLAY-NAME-DUP` (cast `sharedName: true` exempts a role name).
- [Providers and catalog](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/tooling/providers-and-catalog/): Snapshot-first provider resolution, the `--providers` flag, `catalog refresh` re-stamping, and `capabilityVersion`.
- [Editors and LSP](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/tooling/editors/): Installing `lute-lsp`, wiring the VS Code, Neovim, and Oh My Pi clients, and the language features the server provides. dsl 0.26.0: `lute-lsp` reports a replaced binary with one `lute-lsp-stale` diagnostic; `lute doctor --strict`.
- [AI harness guide](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/tooling/ai-harness/): Wiring a trusted `--permission-profile` through `lute context`, `lute check --json`, compile/compile-stream, warning promotion, exit codes, and fixits without letting generated source choose its own authority.
- [Plugin concepts](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/plugins/concepts/): How Lute plugins extend vocabulary and capability surfaces without ever touching the fixed grammar or compiler behavior.
- [Manifests & resolution](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/plugins/manifests/): The `lute.project.yaml` profile graph, the `plugin.yaml` manifest, and how installed plugins resolve into one capability snapshot Occasions may `select: sequence`, reward kinds may `credits:` a state path, and a `cast` export declares the speakers (dsl 0.23.0). dsl 0.24.0: a directive `lower:` is optional, export files reject unknown keys, occasions may declare `judge: before`, and cast entries take `present:`/`emotions:`. dsl 0.26.0: directive attributes typed `{ entity: K }`, reward `target:` contracts (`E-REWARD-TARGET`), cast `sharedName: true`.
- [Typed bridge directives](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/plugins/bridge/): How a plugin declares a typed runtime bridge, the directive that invokes it, and the declared result state it writes.
- [Profiles & activation](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/plugins/profiles/): Selecting capability plugins with a source profile, layering typed options, and distinguishing activation from conjunctive project/host permission ceilings.

## Specification

- [Current specification](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/spec/current/): The consolidated index of what the language enforces today at 0.26.0 — each language area mapped to the proposal that introduced or last changed it, including the `0.26.0` scale and many authors (`E-STATE-DECL-CONFLICT` across documents, duplicate members, `add:` to extend a kind, `defaults.uses` globs, entity-typed directive attributes and `E-REWARD-TARGET`, component `@@who:` / param `default:` / own results, directive `when=`, `target="kind:X"` beats with `occasion.target`, rule-body `count` with `E-RULE-AGGREGATE-CYCLE`, trace/test following `::next` and failing ineligible walks, `W-DISPLAY-NAME-DUP`, `W-ENTRY-WRITE-REREAD`; additive IR), the `0.25.1` performance patch (no language or IR shape change), the `0.25.0` exclusion, shared spends and graph edges (relation `excludes:` with `E-FACT-EXCLUSIVE` / `E-RULE-EXCLUSIVE` and play/trace halting on a violation, `share` keys spent together, bundle `<beat after=…>` edges, `[subquest]` / `[start]` quest anchors, `accept="external"`, `changedOn:`, bridge answers that omit unread fields, `{{x:ordinalWord}}`; additive IR), the `0.24.0` clocks, quest structure and parties (a declared `clock:`, `once: day|slot`, `activate="accept"`, `complete="any"`, `until=`, `failedBy`, entity sub-kinds and `per:` state, cast `present:` with `W-CAST-ABSENT`, `effects: true` components, `::clear`, `bridges:` answers; additive IR), the `0.23.1` patch (`E-QUEST-TIER-MIX` rejects a mixed-tier quest tree; an occasion target domain may narrow to `members:`; no IR shape change), the `0.23.0` author overviews and time (`lute beats`, `lute calendar`, `lute scenario knowledge`, `by=` deadlines, objective targets, `select: sequence`, `also`, lore `<beat>` bundles, `<hub prompt>`, `prev.run`, cast, reward `credits`, a sharper condition decider), the `0.22.0` harness model (engine steps, save seeds, play assertions, derivation by default), run boundaries (`<quest tier>`, entry `once`, `entry.<id>.everRead`), occasion target domains, `owner: engine`, the new default `voiceKey` and component `lineId` scope, the `0.21.1` patch's tightened checks (`E-DUP-VOICEKEY`, `check-project` running the compile) and the optional inlined def body on `ref` placeholders, the `kind: lore` document of looked-up `<entry>` content, quest/lore document bundles, and scene/entry beats answering engine occasions.
- [Specification index](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/spec/): The versioned Lute spec stack — every scenario-DSL revision plus the plugin-system and character-cast proposals, linking the normative repository sources.
- [Normative proposals](https://github.com/journeyWorker/lute/tree/main/docs/proposals): The repository proposal files are the normative source of truth; the website is the readable companion.

## Optional

- [GitHub repository](https://github.com/journeyWorker/lute): Source, issues, and the full history of the Lute language and toolchain.
- [Full-spec showcase](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/examples/showcase/): A walkthrough of the self-contained showcase project exercising every implemented Lute feature end-to-end.
